region.text: Gauda, the land of the chiefs who elected Gopala

ledger.note: 750: the chiefs of Gauda elect Gopala. 'The empire was founded with the election of Gopala by the chiefs of Gauda'; 'Gopala's ascension in 750 CE was a significant political event'; infobox 'Established 750'. The page also says 'late eighth century' and calls the election story Taranatha's, 800 years later.

region.text: Magadha and Bihar, added to the Bengal core

ledger.note: 778: Bihar joins the Pala core. The Pratihara page says Nagabhata II took the plain 'as far as Bihar from the Palas' (after 805), so Bihar was Pala earlier; no page dates the gain, 778 is Cliopatria's year.
785: Dhruva reaches the Doab. 'Dhruva met and defeated Dharmapala in the Doab'; the struggle is dated 785-816 and the battle is not.
790: Dhruva goes home. He 'returned to the South in 790'.

region.text: the kingdom of Kannauj under Chakrayudha

ledger.note: c. 791: Dharmapala takes Kannauj and sets his brother on its throne. Dharmapala was 'invading the kingdom of Kannauj around 791', defeated Indrayudha and installed his brother Chakrayudha as a vassal (the Khalimpur plate, regnal year 32, records it without a CE date).
800: Govinda III's northern campaign. Chakrayudha surrendered to him and Dharmapala also submitted (both undated on this page); the Govinda III page dates the campaign to 800.
800: the campaign over; no page gives a later date and the Rashtrakutas did not stay.

c. 810: the king of Pragjyotisha submits to Devapala. 'Pragjyotisa or Assam accepted the suzerainty of Devapala' (Pala Empire page); the Devapala page lists the invasion of Pragjyotisha, also undated. 810 is Devapala's accession on Majumdar's column (810-c. 850; Sircar 812, Ganguly 806), the bridge year of kamarupa-kingdom /ledger/14, whose mirror this is (an earlier version here stood at 825). Drawn as a vassal tint, not direct rule: Cliopatria's shape never reaches Assam.

816: Nagabhata II takes Kannauj. 'In 816, Nagabhata II invaded the Doab, and defeated king Chakrayudha', proclaimed himself King of Kannauj; Ayudha control ended. The Monghyr defeat of Dharmapala comes after, undated.

825: Devapala's conquest of Utkala. The Devapala page lists 'the Utkala (present-day Northern Odisha) whose king fled from his capital city' without a date; 825 is the year Cliopatria's shape reaches Odisha. The state is the Bhauma-Kara kingdom of Toshala: its page says 'a series of Rashtrakuta and Pala invasions weakened and disintegrated the Bhauma kingdom' (names no king and no year; its Dhenkanal inscription of c. 846 shows a kingdom 'in a bad shape'). Drawn as a vassal tint, not direct rule.

c. 860: the Odisha tint ends. 'Narayanapala lost control of Assam and Orissa' (Pala Empire page, undated). 860 is Narayanapala's accession on Sircar's column (860-917; Majumdar 854, Chowdhury 866, Ganguly 873, which the ruler strip follows) and the year kamarupa-kingdom /ledger/15 uses. An earlier version stood at 840, inside Devapala's reign.

c. 860: the Pragjyotisha tint ends. 'Narayanapala lost control of Assam and Orissa'; 'Encouraged by the Pala decline, the King Harjara of Assam assumed imperial titles' (Pala Empire page, both undated). 860 as for Orissa and as kamarupa-kingdom /ledger/15, the mirror. An earlier version stood at 840.

region.text: Varendra, lost to the Kaivarta rebels

ledger.note: 1072: Varendra rises against Mahipala II. 'Divya (or, Dibyak) killed him and occupied the Varendra region' (Pala Empire page); 'after Mahipala's death at the hands of Kaivarta chief Divya' (Ramapala page). Neither page dates it; 1072 is the year Cliopatria's shape loses Bengal and the first year of Ramapala on the page's Sircar column. The land is Varendra only: the Ramapala page has him reigning at the very beginning 'over a small territory comprising part of Magadha and Radha', so Radha stays in the keyframes (an earlier version of this event took all of Bengal, 141,371 km2).

ledger.note: 1072: the Varmans hold east Bengal. 'The Varmans occupied eastern Bengal during his reign' (Pala Empire page, of Vigrahapala III, whose reign the page's five chronologies give as 1043-1070 Sircar and Ganguly, 1054-1072 Majumdar, 1058-1075 Chowdhury, 1050-1076 Sinha); 1072 is Cliopatria's year and falls in three of the five. Ramapala 'kept the Sens in check, but lost Mithila to a Karnataka chief named Nanyadeva' who 'formed his own kingdom based out of Mithila which became known as the Karnats of Mithila' (Ramapala page; the Pala page says 'Karnat chief'). Neither page dates it; 1085 is the year Cliopatria's shape drops north Bihar (33,636 km2, 24,531 of it in Bihar), a bridge inside Ramapala's reign (1077-1130).

region.text: Varendra: the Rajshahi and Rangpur divisions

ledger.note: 1085: Ramapala recovers Varendra. 'After gaining control of Varendra' and 'He crushed the Varendra Rebellion' (Ramapala page); the rebels held 'the Varendra region' (Pala Empire page). None of it is dated, so 1085 is a bridge inside his reign (1077-1130). Radha is not part of the gain: the page has him hold it from the start, so it stays in the keyframes from 1072.

ledger.note: c. 1100: Ramapala takes western Kamarupa. 'He brought Kamarupa and Rarh under his control' (Ramapala page; 'Kamarupa and Rar', Pala Empire page), undated. 1100 and the region are those of kamarupa-kingdom /ledger/26 (confidence 2 there, the end of Jaya Pala's reign); here a bridge inside Ramapala's reign, confidence 1. region.text: western Kamarupa: Kamarupanagara and the lower Brahmaputra

ledger.note: 1126: Vaidyadeva's separate kingdom. 'The rebellion was crushed by Vaidyadeva, minister of Kumarapala' and 'after Kumarapala's death, Vaidyadeva practically created a separate kingdom' (Pala Empire page). Kumarapala reigns 1126-1128 in the ruler strip (Ganguly); 1126 is the year of kamarupa-kingdom /ledger/27, whose mirror this is.

1159: the Senas hold a part of Varendra. 'Their territory had expanded to include Vanga and a part of Varendra by the end of Vijayasena's reign' (to 1159, infobox). Only the Varendra part is drawn as Pala land lost: the page does not say Vanga was taken from the Palas, and after 1072 the Pala keyframes no longer hold east Bengal (the Varmans, ledger 1072). Ballala Sena then took Gaur (undated). Confidence 2: the year is the page's, the Rajshahi division is a reading of 'a part of Varendra'.

ledger.note: 1161: the Pala dynasty ends. Infobox 'Disestablished 1161'; the Sena page says 'the Palas were ousted in totality, and their entire territory annexed sometime after 1165'; a Gaya line (Govindapala, Palapala) lasted to about 1200.

wars.name: Tripartite struggle for Kannauj
wars.outcome: Dhruva beat Dharmapala in the Doab (home in 790); Dharmapala installed Chakrayudha at Kannauj around 791; Govinda III received Dharmapala's submission in 800; 'In 816, Nagabhata II invaded the Doab, and defeated king Chakrayudha'. 'At the Battle of Monghyr, Nagabhata's forces soundly defeated those of Dharmapala', undated.
wars.note: The struggle ended with Pratihara control of Kannauj; the Palas kept Bengal and Bihar.

wars.name: Pratihara advance on Bihar
wars.outcome: Nagabhata II defeated Dharmapala at Monghyr and took the plain 'as far as Bihar from the Palas'; Bhoja later 'defeated the Pala emperor Narayanapala after Devapala's death'. None of it is dated; 833 is the end of Nagabhata II's reign on the Pratihara page.
wars.note: The span is the reign of Nagabhata II (805-833) from 816; the Bhoja defeat is later and undated.

wars.note: The Bangar charter's claim is cited on the Kamboja page; Chandella and Chandra invasions came before.

wars.name: Chola invasions of Bengal
wars.outcome: Rajendra Chola I 'frequently invaded Bengal from 1021 to 1023 CE to get Ganges water'; Mahipala I's rule was 'temporarily hampered'. No border moved.
wars.note: The Kamboja page has Dharmapala of Dandabhukti defeated by Rajendra I in the 11th century.

wars.name: Varendra rebellion

zones.text: Varendra: the Rajshahi and Rangpur divisions

wars.outcome: Mahipala II was killed, Shurapala ruled two years, and Ramapala recovered Varendra from Bhima and Divya; none of the events is dated on the page.
wars.note: The span is a bridge: the Ramapala page gives no years at all for the rebellion.

wars.name: Sena conquest of Pala Bengal
wars.outcome: By 1159 the Senas held Vanga and a part of Varendra; Ballala Sena took Gaur; 'the Palas were ousted in totality' sometime after 1165.
wars.note: The start is Vijayasena's accession on the page (1096); no page dates the first clash.

wars.name: Pala-Gahadavala conflict over Munger
wars.outcome: 'Madanapala captured Munger from the Gahadavalas'; undated, so the span is his reign (Ganguly 1143-1161).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier is recorded on the pages opened; the Gangetic plain frontier with the Pratiharas and the Bengal frontier with the Kambojas, Chandras and Senas are approximate throughout.

notes: Pala Empire, Cliopatria 'Pala Empire' 750-1168 (25 shapes), nine Wikipedia pages (the budget); the Govinda III page (opened for the Rashtrakuta dossier) dates the 800 campaign and is cited in the note of one event only. The Wikipedia pages date almost nothing for the Palas: Dharmapala and Devapala say 'undated' about every conquest, the Ramapala page dates only his reign and death, so most of the correction work rests on page statements that contradict a Cliopatria shape, not on dates. The infobox gives no area. Cliopatria rows to correct: 778-782, 788-805, 814-824 and 840-859 draw Kannauj, Awadh and the Doab as Pala land; 825-839 (1.36 M km2, Punjab to Odisha) is a panegyric extent, replaced by the core; 947-989 should lose northern and eastern Bengal until 981; 1085-1168 omits Radha and Varendra, which the Ramapala page and the capital at Ramavati put in Pala hands. Disagreements: five reign chronologies on the Pala page (the ruler strip follows Ganguly 1994); the page says both 'late eighth century' and 750; the infobox lists Govindapala as 1139-1161 against his body dates 1158-1165; Mahipala I 978-1026 on his page against 988-1038 in its succession box; Sena page 1070 for the dynasty, 1095 for Hemanta, 1096-1159 for Vijayasena, with Palas ousted 'after 1165' against an infobox end of 1161 here. Not dated on any page (left out or confidence 1): Bihar's acquisition (778 is Cliopatria's); the Kamboja invasion of Gauda; the Varendra rebellion and its end; Ramavati's founding; Madanapala's capture of Munger; Ramapala's control of Kamarupa and Rarh (his page); the Mithila loss to Nanyadeva; the loss of Magadha to Vallabharaja of Bodh Gaya; Nepal as a vassal (Dharmapala page, a tradition); Sarnath renovations in 1026; the Himalayan gain of 839-848 (Tibetan control lost, in Devapala's reign). The Ramapala page speaks of a rebel state of Varendra (Divya, Bhima): no page opened dates it, so no rebel dossier was written; the counterpart slug kaivarta-rebels-of-varendra is a placeholder for the gap-filler, who should open 'Varendra Rebellion'. Cliopatria's Sena row draws Bengal (86 percent) from 1072, against the Sena page (Radha samantas of the Palas from 1070, Vanga and part of Varendra only by 1159): the Sena group should check it. Counterparts needing dossiers: kamboja-pala-dynasty (north-west Bengal, 10th-11th c.), kaivarta-rebels-of-varendra, Ayudha dynasty of Kannauj (Indrayudha, Chakrayudha), Utkala. Gazetteer names wanted: Varendra, Radha, Gauda (alias of Bengal exists), Pundravardhana, Munger, Ramavati, Dandabhukti, Kamarupa (alias exists). REPAIR RUN (2026-10-19, after the adversarial review; pages reopened: Pala Empire, Ramapala, and Bhauma-Kara dynasty as the one new page). (1) 947-980 now use the 900 shape minus Bangladesh, because Cliopatria's 947 and 980 shapes also drop north Bihar (82,951 km2) and south-west Bengal (43,246 km2) that no page takes away; 981-1055 and 1072-1161 keep Radha (the West Bengal land of the 900 shape, 52,856 km2) because Cliopatria's 1000 shape has only 27,060 km2 of West Bengal and the Ramapala page has him hold 'part of Magadha and Radha' from the start. The reviewer proposed union(Pala 1072, West Bengal); the whole admin-1 would add 48.8 thousand km2 of West Bengal at 1072 with no event, so the dossier keeps the 900-shape Radha instead. (2) New events: 1056 gain from kamarupa-kingdom (mirror of its /ledger/22), 1072 loss of east Bengal to the Varmans (Vigrahapala III's reign is 1054-1072, 1058-1075 and 1050-1076 on three of the five columns), 1072 loss of the Meghalaya, Assam, Tripura and north-east Bihar edges to nobody, 1085 loss of Mithila to the Karnats (undated on both pages), 1100 gain and 1126 loss of western Kamarupa (mirrors of kamarupa-kingdom /ledger/26 and /27; two new keyframes 1100-1110 and 1126-1146, the 1085 and 1111 corrections apply to 1085-1099 and 1111-1125). (3) The 1072 Varendra loss, the 1085 Varendra gain and the 1159 Sena loss are restricted to Varendra (Rajshahi and Rangpur; Rajshahi alone for the Senas): the pages say the rebels held 'the Varendra region' and Vijayasena held 'Vanga and a part of Varendra', and Vanga was Varman land, not Pala land in these keyframes. (4) Narayanapala's loss of Assam and Orissa moved from 840 to 860 (Sircar's accession year and kamarupa-kingdom /ledger/15); Devapala's Pragjyotisha tint moved from 825 to 810 (kamarupa-kingdom /ledger/14); Utkala stays at 825 (Cliopatria's year). The counterpart 'Utkala (Odisha)' became bhauma-kara-dynasty. (5) Left as Cliopatria draws them (thin, no page dates them): +14,162 km2 at 1111, -14,162 at 1147 and -13,151 at 1152 (Jharkhand and Nepal edge; Madanapala's capture of Munger from the Gahadavalas is undated); 4,805 km2 gained and 6,322 km2 lost at 981 at the Bihar, Nepal and Assam edge. Open questions for a gap-filler: Gauda (Malda and Murshidabad) lay in Kamboja hands on the Pala page ('Gauda had been lost to the Kambojas') yet the 947-980 keyframes keep West Bengal as Pala; the Karnat dynasty and Varman dynasty pages were not opened (budget), so the Mithila and east-Bengal years are bridges; Ramapala's suzerainty over the Varman king has no vassal_start because nothing dates its end. Counterpart placeholders now in the ledger: bhauma-kara-dynasty, kamboja-pala-dynasty, kaivarta-rebels-of-varendra, varman-dynasty-of-east-bengal, karnat-dynasty-of-mithila; chandra-dynasty, kamarupa-kingdom and sena-dynasty are Cliopatria rows.
